steps.instruction: Add one new public method to the WatchlistStore class: `clearWatched(): void`. Contract: (a) it removes every item whose `watched` flag is `true` from the list — all watched items removed as a single update; (b) items with `watched === false` must remain, keeping their relative order; (c) if no item is watched, the call is a no-op and the list is unchanged; (d) after the call, the `items`, `count` and `watchedCount` signals must reflect the new list, and persistence must behave exactly like the existing `remove(id)` method (same storage write, performed as part of the call, synchronously); (e) do NOT change the signature or behaviour of the constructor, `add`, `remove`, `toggleWatched`, `items`, `count` or `watchedCount` — every existing test must keep passing. Add your own unit tests in src/app/watchlist-store.spec.ts for clearWatched: mixed list keeps only unwatched items; all watched empties the list; none watched is a no-op. Other units are being told about this exact signature in the same round, so it will be available on the injected store.

input.reason: tsc is clean and 38/41 tests pass. The 3 failures are: (1) watchlist-store.clearWatched is correct in memory but leaves the persisted state empty/unreadable — a freshly constructed store loads nothing instead of the remaining unwatched items; (2)+(3) my own watchlist acceptance tests crashed on their own TestBed setup: the template legitimately uses routerLink, which needs ActivatedRoute (NG0201), and my test module did not provide router services. So one step fixes the store's persistence write (same key, same serialization, same write path as remove(), performed synchronously), and one step attaches a corrected watchlist acceptance test that adds provideRouter([]) — no watchlist code change is expected.

steps.instruction: Your clearWatched() in-memory behaviour is correct (watched items removed, unwatched kept in order, no-op when nothing is watched) — those tests all pass. Do NOT change the signal logic. The bug is persistence: the acceptance test 'persists the cleared list so a fresh store loads only the unwatched items' fails — after add(1), add(2), toggleWatched(2), clearWatched(), a newly constructed WatchlistStore loads an EMPTY list instead of [item 1]. The stored data after clearWatched() is ending up empty or unreadable — typical causes: writing an empty array, deleting the storage key (removeItem), writing to a different key or with a different serialization than the rest of the store, or deferring the write (effect/microtask/timeout) so it never happens during the call. Fix ONLY the persistence part of clearWatched(): during the call, synchronously, write exactly the remaining unwatched items to the SAME storage key with the SAME serialization, through the SAME write helper/code path that add, remove and toggleWatched already use. Do NOT delete the storage key when unwatched items remain; an empty stored list is correct only when the remaining list is genuinely empty. After the fix: with items [A (watched === false), B (watched === true)], clearWatched() must leave storage containing exactly [A], and a freshly constructed WatchlistStore must then load exactly [A] with watched === false. Add a regression test to your own spec reproducing this scenario (add two items, toggle one watched, clearWatched(), then construct a second store instance and assert it loads only the unwatched item). Do not change add, remove, toggleWatched, items, count, watchedCount, the constructor, or the KEY value; every existing test must keep passing.

No code change is required from you this round. Your clear-watched button from round 1 is correct — the two acceptance-test failures for your unit were caused by the test harness itself, not by your code: the acceptance test's TestBed provided only WatchlistStore, so the routerLink directives your template legitimately uses could not resolve ActivatedRoute (NG0201). The attached corrected acceptance test adds provideRouter([]) to the TestBed providers, which supplies the router services your template needs. Keep your implementation exactly as it is; do not change your component, template, styles or any existing test. Only if the corrected acceptance test still reveals an actual defect in the button should you fix it, without altering any existing behaviour.
